name: Cross-Border eCommerce Returns
title: Cross-Border eCommerce Returns: Recover Duty | TDR
description: Cross-border eCommerce returns can cost you duty twice. See how duty drawback and Returned Goods Relief recover duties in the US, EU and UK.
hero-title: Cross-Border eCommerce Returns<br><span class="text-samaritanGreen">Without Paying Duty Twice</span>
hero-description: Every cross-border return carries a customs cost. Recover the duty you already paid and avoid paying it again.
page-title: Returns should not be a <span class="text-samaritanYellow">customs cost you pay twice.</span>
page-description: When an international customer returns an order, the duty paid on the way in is lost unless you claim it back, and goods coming back can be charged again. Duty drawback and Returned Goods Relief recover or avoid that cost in the US, EU and UK.

card1.title: The return crosses the border
card1.description: Customer returns, exchanges and rejected orders move goods back across customs borders, with duty questions at every crossing.

card2.title: Duty is paid, then lost
card2.description: Duty paid when the order was imported is not refunded automatically when the goods go back.

card3.title: Two routes recover it
card3.description: Duty drawback refunds duty on imported goods that leave again. Returned Goods Relief avoids duty on goods that were exported and come back.

conditions-title: Where cross-border returns cost you money
conditions-intro: A cross-border return is not only a shipping cost. It is a chain of customs events, and each one can add cost if it is not managed.
conditions-item1: Duty paid on the original import is not refunded when the customer sends the goods back, unless you claim it.
conditions-item2: Goods returned to the market they were exported from can be charged duty again if relief is not claimed at re-import.
conditions-item3: Returned items cannot be matched to their original shipment, so claims lack evidence.
conditions-item4: Time limits are missed: drawback and Returned Goods Relief each have deadlines that run from import or export.
conditions-item5: Worn or tried-on items come back and cannot qualify for Returned Goods Relief.
conditions-callout-description: Returns can generate 6-8% cost savings on original import duties. In the US, drawback can recover up to 99% of duties paid. In the EU and the UK, 100% of duties and VAT can be recovered.
how-it-works-title: How Duty Recovery on Returns<span class="text-samaritanDarkGreen"> Works</span>
how-it-works-description: TDR connects each return to its original shipment and customs declaration, identifies which route applies, and prepares the claim.
how-it-works-label: Estimate what your returns could recover

how-it-works-step1.title: Trace the original movement
how-it-works-step1.description: Identify when the goods were imported or exported, and under which customs declaration.

how-it-works-step2.title: Match the return
how-it-works-step2.description: Link each returned item to that movement using order, product and transport records. Product identifiers help identify exactly which items are being returned.

how-it-works-step3.title: Choose the route and claim
how-it-works-step3.description: Apply duty drawback or Returned Goods Relief, depending on how the goods moved, and file the claim with the supporting evidence.

how-it-works-callout.title: Already paid duty on returns?
how-it-works-callout.description: Don’t assume the opportunity is lost. Keep your import, export and return records and let us review whether a recovery opportunity may exist.
how-it-works-callout.label: Contact TDR

ecom-title: Returns in apparel, sporting goods and luxury
ecom-intro: The same customs rules apply to every product, but the way returns behave differs by sector.
ecom-list-title: What to watch in your sector
ecom-item1: Apparel and sporting goods: high return volumes make item-level records essential. Worn or tried-on items are not eligible for Returned Goods Relief.
ecom-item2: Luxury goods: higher unit values mean each return carries more duty, so each unmatched return costs more.
ecom-item3: Multiple warehouses and carriers: returns pass through several hands, and the records need to be joined before a claim.
ecom-item4: Marketplaces and 3PLs: the party importing the returned goods may not be the party that exported them, which affects VAT relief in the UK and in the EU.
ecom-item5: Exchanges and partial returns: only the returned items can be claimed, so claims need to be item-level.
ecom-description: TDR connects the outbound shipment to the return, identifies which returns qualify and prepares the evidence. If duty has already been paid, we review whether it can be recovered.
compare-title: Which route applies in the US, EU and UK?
compare-intro: The route depends on how the goods moved. Duty drawback applies to goods imported and later sent back abroad. Returned Goods Relief applies to goods that were exported and come back.
eligibility-description: The direction of the goods, timing, condition and available evidence all matter. Start with a quick review of one return flow.

faq_1_question: How do cross-border returns affect my customs costs?
faq_1_answer: When a customer returns an order across a border, the duty paid on the way in is not refunded automatically, and goods coming back to the market they were exported from can be charged again if relief is not claimed. Recovering that cost requires the right customs route and evidence.
faq_2_question: How can I recover duties on cross-border returns?
faq_2_answer: Two routes apply, depending on how the goods moved. Duty drawback refunds duty paid on imported goods that are later exported again. Returned Goods Relief gives relief from duty on goods that were exported and come back. TDR assesses which route fits each flow.
faq_3_question: What is the difference between duty drawback and Returned Goods Relief?
faq_3_answer: Duty drawback is a refund of duty that was previously paid. Returned Goods Relief gives relief from duty when qualifying goods are re-imported. See our pages on duty drawback in the US, EU and UK, and on Returned Goods Relief in the EU and UK. American Goods Returned applies only to goods made in the US. Returned Goods Relief applies to goods that were in free circulation before being exported.
faq_4_question: How much can I recover on returns?
faq_4_answer: In the US, drawback can recover up to 99% of duties paid. In the EU and the UK, 100% of duties and VAT can be recovered. Returns can generate 6-8% cost savings on original import duties.
faq_5_question: Are worn or tried-on items eligible?
faq_5_answer: Not for Returned Goods Relief. Goods must come back in the same state: not used, not tried and not worn.
faq_6_question: How long does it take to receive refunds?
faq_6_answer: CBP processes US drawback claims in 3-12 months on average. In the EU, customs authorities process claims in 3-5 months on average. In the UK, HMRC processes claims in 1-3 months on average. These timeframes are based on observation and are not a commitment from customs authorities.
faq_7_question: Which records do I need to claim duty on returns?
faq_7_answer: Import and export declarations, commercial invoices, transport documents, and return records that link each returned item to the original order. Product identifiers help identify exactly which items are being returned and provide a source for the refund.
faq_8_question: Is there a minimum budget or an upfront cost?
faq_8_answer: No. TDR has no budget threshold, and success-based fees mean you pay only when recovery succeeds.
